subject.title: Create Claw agent and root install record

question: Should OpenClaw accept the experimental Claws root-install lifecycle—persistent `claw_installs` ownership, resumable partial phases, and consent-bound agent/workspace mutation—as a core-supported stack after its parent schema/plan slice lands?
rationale: The patch is not a narrow bug fix: it establishes a durable core lifecycle and public CLI mutation contract whose final owner, rollout sequence, and follow-on status/remove semantics require maintainer product and compatibility intent.

options.title: Sponsor the stacked lifecycle
options.body: Approve the parent-to-child stack order and retain this consent-bound, resumable SQLite ownership model as the canonical experimental Claws foundation.

options.title: Keep Claws read-only for now
options.body: Land or retain only planning work until a core owner defines the complete install, recovery, status, and removal lifecycle.

options.title: Redirect the design
options.body: Ask for a narrower owner-approved lifecycle boundary before accepting persistent root-install state in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the stacked lifecycle
recommendation.body: Approve the parent-to-child stack order and retain this consent-bound, resumable SQLite ownership model as the canonical experimental Claws foundation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comments cover the relevant user-state, path-safety, and durable-schema invariants and provide the clearest available routing signal.
